validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real and current. TC Energy Corp.'s own May 1, 2026 Q1-2026 results release (tcenergy.com / GlobeNewswire, dateline CALGARY) states verbatim: 'Approved the Appalachia Supply Project with an expected build multiple of 7.3x: an expansion project of our Columbia Gas system designed to provide up to 0.8 Bcf/d of capacity to facilitate expanded new natural gas-fired power generation. The project has an anticipated in-service date of 2030 and an estimated project cost of approximately US$1.5 billion.' Independently corroborated (separate origin, separate reporter) by Oil & Gas Journal ('TC Energy expanding Columbia Gas system with 800-MMcfd Appalachia Supply project', Christopher E. Smith, 2026-05-05) and Pipeline & Gas Journal ('TC Energy Approves $1.5 Billion Columbia Gas Expansion to Boost U.S. Power Demand'). Also picked up by Natural Gas Intelligence, Marcellus Drilling News (paywalled beyond teaser) and BNN Bloomberg. Not a GEM-only entity; this is not a hallucination. COLUMBIA FAMILY DISCRIMINATOR: this is the INTERSTATE Columbia Gas Transmission LLC (TC Energy/GIP), not the NiSource LDC Columbia Gas of Ohio -- TC Energy's own release names it as 'our Columbia Gas system' in a Q1 TC Energy Corp. earnings release; no FERC docket or LDC/OPSB filing found for this project at all yet (see Construction/spec units -- still pre-filing). CLASSIFICATION: Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are both correct -- this is an expansion (added mainline capacity + compression) of the FERC-jurisdictional interstate Columbia Gas Transmission system, not a gathering/distribution line. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 46-row roster and specifically the other three Columbia Gas Transmission rows (P3189 Marysville Connector, P4446 Virginia Electrification, P4447 Northern Loop) -- all are separate, distinctly named, already-existing proposed/shelved projects on the same parent system; Appalachia Supply Project is a distinct, newly announced (May 2026) scope with its own $1.5B/800 MMcf/d/2030 profile. No overlap. OWNERSHIP: entity match to the existing Columbia Gas Transmission LLC entity used by P3189/P4446/P4447 (100% Owner1, ParentEntityIDs E100001014494, Parent = TC Energy Corp 60% / Global Infrastructure Partners 40%) -- staged onto the Owner/Operator tab as REFS_ADDED with the same entity spelling per entity_lookup convention. STATUS: proposed is correct as recorded -- TC Energy's own language is 'Approved' at the internal capital-allocation/board level (a positive FID-type signal) but no FERC certificate application, notice of intent, or pre-filing docket for 'Appalachia Supply Project' by that name could be found (checked Federal Register 2026 Columbia Gas Transmission notices and general FERC-docket web search); no construction start reported. This matches GEM's 'proposed' tier, not 'construction'. See status_reviews[] and fills[] for full sourcing of each unit.

validity.researcher_notes: Database defect, not a research finding about the pipeline: the tracker row reads RouteType='Mapped route (at any accuracy)' while RouteAccuracy='no route', and the routes repo's own P7999.geojson (../GOIT-GGIT-pipeline-routes/data/individual-routes/gas-pipelines/P7999.geojson) is a FeatureCollection with a single feature whose geometry is null -- there is no merged geometry at all. This is exactly the three-way-sync violation the CARDINAL RULE (RouteType/RouteAccuracy/routes-repo must always agree) exists to catch: a null-geometry file cannot support 'Mapped route (at any accuracy)'. I did not set RouteType to 'Capacity expansion only' (the value used on this batch's other LengthKnown=0 compression-only rows, e.g. P2538/P2651/P3169/P7825/P7813/P7829) because I could not confirm from any source whether Appalachia Supply Project involves new looped pipe or is compression-only -- TC Energy's language ('additional compression and minor modifications') describes the PATH to the 2.0 Bcf/d future phases, not necessarily the scope of the initial 0.8 Bcf/d phase this row records, and Length/Diameter are both genuinely unresolved (see fills[]), not confirmed zero. 'Unavailable (cannot find route)' is the accurate, non-committal correction; RouteAccuracy='no route' already reads correctly and needs no change.
